rule: Budgets are fixed before measuring and never adjusted after results, except by an explicit, dated amendment recorded in `amendments` with its reason and the measurements it rests on. A missing measurement is not a pass. Speedups must keep output byte-identical.

laptop.machine: MacBook Pro M5 Max, quiet (load1 < 2.0, no foreign build or benchmark)

workload.description: warm daemon v2 session, 12-turn EN/DE history (~32 KiB), new message with PII sized uniformly 512-4096 bytes, gaze setup policy written by the binary itself, strict restore. Cold start: spawn to first validated clean with a warm page cache, at least 5 runs, maximum reported.

server.machine: Amp orb a1.medium: 4 vCPU (shared, not dedicated), 8 GB, x86-64 Linux, x86-64 release binary built in the orb. Replaces the originally decided Hetzner CCX23 (4 dedicated vCPU, 16 GB, Debian 13), which was not rented. Same architecture, OS family and vCPU count; half the memory, still over 3x the 2.5 GB peak budget. Shared vCPUs make it at most as fast and noisier than a CCX23, so a pass here is conservative; budget numbers are unchanged.

workload.description: as laptop, with 4 sessions on one resident daemon; each step sends the 4 sessions' frames as one simultaneous burst, so per-turn latency includes queueing behind the other sessions

amendments.unchanged: laptop turn p95 500 ms and p99 1000 ms, reclean, restore, cold start and RSS budgets; every server budget
amendments.reason: No byte-identical path reaches a 150 ms single-session p50 with the Nym safety net on, as the setup profile keeps it. Per-request inference reuse halves model work, and more Nym intra-op threads keep output identical but make Nym only 1.3-1.5x faster; concurrency does not move a single session's p50. 250 ms stays within the budget's own basis: Gaze adds at most about 10% to a 4.2 s model call, about 420 ms. Dropping the neutral Nym view, a smaller or int8 or CoreML Nym model, and dropping NER from the warm turn were ruled out for 1.0 because each weakens detection or the Trust axis.

measurements.main_9ff7ad9_laptop_indicative: 31 quiet samples, not a gate receipt: turn p50 1117 ms, p90 1745 ms, max 3131 ms
measurements.main_9ff7ad9_server_receipt: a1.medium orb, quiet, F8 FAIL: turn p50 11383 ms, p95 21346 ms, p99 27493 ms, reclean p95 97785 ms, restore p95 9.6 ms, cold start max 3467 ms, peak RSS 829820928 bytes
measurements.cached_turn_profile: perf-timers build with request-wide NER and Nym reuse, 4 seeds, laptop at load1 5-7: turn 314-801 ms (median about 445 ms) with 1 Nym thread, median about 340 ms with 4 or 8 threads and identical output digests; Nym is about 75% of a turn
measurements.estimate: quiet single-session p50 about 220-260 ms with reuse plus more Nym threads; about 150-190 ms only with parallel Nym windows on shared-weight sessions, which is a follow-up

amendments.server_condition: The server budgets stay as decided. After concurrent session cleaning lands and is re-measured, if the server envelope misses only on turn p50, its p50 may be raised by a further dated amendment with the same reasoning, but never above 420 ms.

amendments.unchanged: every budget number in both envelopes; the laptop envelope still gates the release
amendments.reason: For 1.0 the server envelope is a published, measured receipt and does not gate the release. One session with no queue already uses about 2.4 of the 4 vCPUs, so a turn costs about 3 CPU-seconds and a 4-session burst cannot finish much under 3 s however it is scheduled. Reaching the 250 ms p50 needs about 12x less work per turn, and even the 420 ms ceiling from the first amendment needs about 7x. Concurrent session cleaning in the daemon or sharding sessions across processes would gain at most about 1.2x, so neither was built. Dropping the neutral Nym view, a smaller Nym model, and a different server workload or hardware stay ruled out for 1.0.

measurements.single_session_server: same binary, concurrency 1, 16 samples: turn p50 1284 ms, max 5981 ms, reclean median about 14.5 s; daemon CPU 2.37 cores averaged over 25 s

amendments.reinstate: The server envelope gates the release again once the post-1.0 work that cuts per-turn CPU lands (Nym windows per turn first, then reclean), with a fresh quiet server receipt.
